title: Briefing – Friday, 27 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: relief bounce in Asia and US futures after a bruising week, but AI doubts persist. Kospi up 3.8%, Nikkei up 2.0%, S&P future up 1.8%, Nasdaq future up 2.8%; Nasdaq 100 down 3.9% over five days.
- Nvidia turmoil headlines (credit rating on watch, shares down) and Nvidia-Kioxia memory tie-up as an alternative to Korean chips, a question mark behind the Kospi jump.
- Copper up 7.0% to 5.70, gold up 4.1% to about 3,680: growth and protection bid together. China profits are two-speed, AI winners versus weak consumption and real estate.
- Energy: Brent 92.8 (down 1.9%), TTF 87.6 (up 3.7% on the week), Kuwait drone attack; margin headwind for European industry.
- Rates: US 10-year 4.85% (down 5.6bp); Bund 10-year 3.3% (up 3bp), 2-year 3.06% (up 4bp). De Cos named ECB chief, continuity.
- Europe closed up yesterday (DAX up 2.1%, Stoxx 600 up 1.8%) on easing tariff fears; new US tariff threats on 14 partners are a risk.
- Sensitivity model (rule of thumb, R-squared 0.22): Stoxx 600 about +53bp. Tailwinds: commodities, tech, industrials, luxury. Headwinds: healthcare, telecom, utilities, real estate.
- VIX 26.8 (down 5.3%), still elevated; Black Friday thin liquidity.

title: Briefing – Thursday, 26 November 2026
notes:
- Theme: Asian bounce (Kospi +1.3%, Hang Seng +2.1%, Nikkei +1.7%) inside a drawdown; Kospi still -7.4% over five days.
- Driver chain: Brent -3.8% to about $91 and US 10-year down 5.6bp to 4.85% ease inflation and valuation pressure, supporting tech.
- Risk: S&P warned of a one-notch Nvidia downgrade over governance risk; Nasdaq 100 -0.6%, VIX up 7.3% to 28.3.
- Inflation backdrop: PCE expected at 3.8% for October; BoK hiked 25bp to 3.25%; a BOJ policymaker flagged faster hikes.
- Gold +2.6% (~$3,627) and copper +3.4%: mixed signals on protection versus demand.
- Europe: Stoxx 600 -1.1%, DAX -1.3%, Euro Stoxx 50 -1.8%; Bund 10-year 3.27%; TTF gas ~87, up 8% over five days.
- Model (historical rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 +54bp expected, commodities and tech and luxury favored; telecom, healthcare, utilities lag. Low R-squared.
- Watch: EU tariff escalation, Nvidia rating, hot inflation data pushing yields up.

title: Briefing – Wednesday, 25 November 2026
notes:
- Main chain: Wall Street AI wobble (Nasdaq 100 down 2.0%) leads to Asian tech rout (Kospi down 5.9%, Nikkei down 2.8%, SoftBank down 15%), then to a risk-off tone in European tech and cyclicals.
- Earnings read-through: Dell sales more than doubled on AI servers, $25B buyback, stock up. HPE record growth, raised guide, stock down. Micron down on BNP oversupply warning. Anthropic below its $83 IPO price. Takeaway: demand is strong, but the market questions pricing and a possible supply glut.
- Rates: the US 10-year is at 4.90% (down 1.4bp), the Bund 10-year at 3.31% (down 4bp). Japan services inflation at a 36-year high, Australian core inflation at a two-year high, Fed's Williams points to higher rates over time. Bonds are not offering a cushion.
- Oil: Brent down 4.5% to $87.3, helps margins and inflation. TTF gas $91.7, up 7.3% over five days, a headwind for European industry.
- Gold down 5.3% and copper down 4.0% over five days, which looks like broad risk reduction rather than a flight to safety. VIX at 26.4.
- Sensitivity model (rule of thumb, low R2): Stoxx 600 about minus 28bp; tech vs market minus 40bp, industrials minus 31bp; healthcare plus 39bp, telecom plus 27bp, insurance plus 12bp, real estate plus 11bp, utilities plus 6bp.
- Healthcare: Sanofi buying Insmed (biggest pharma deal in three years, Insmed up 14%) signals the sector is hunting growth ahead of patent cliffs.
- Risks and swing factors: Nvidia and Huang hearings, Houthi attack on the PIF tower, Russia-Estonia tensions. Defensives may be crowded if tech stabilizes.

title: Briefing – Tuesday, 24 November 2026
notes:
- Dominant theme: Huang's return to Nvidia triggered a huge relief rally. S&P 500 up 4.7 percent, Nasdaq 100 up 6.9 percent, Nvidia up more than 30 percent, after a 10 percent Nasdaq drop last week.
- Asia: Kospi up 7.0 percent, Nikkei up 4.1 percent, Hang Seng down 0.3 percent and down 5.1 percent over five days. An AI-supply-chain rally, not a broad one.
- Complication: Fed's Williams signals more hikes possible. US 10-year yield at 4.9 percent, dollar firm, housing frozen. Congress is critical of the Huang decision; Megaspeed blacklisted.
- VIX down 25.8 percent but still 26.6, so relief rather than calm.
- Oil and gas: Brent down 3.9 percent to 85.9 dollars, but Hormuz tanker mine incidents add risk. TTF gas up 1.5 percent to about 89.7. Copper down 2.4 percent, gold down 0.6 percent.
- Europe: Stoxx 600 up 1.8 percent Monday but down 3.8 percent over five days. Model rule of thumb: about plus 94 basis points, R-squared 0.22.
- Sector lean: industrials (plus 40 bp) and tech (plus 24 bp) tend to benefit. Oil and gas (minus 84 bp), utilities and telecom (minus 27 bp each), commodities (minus 24 bp), health care (minus 14 bp) tend to lag.
- Earnings and watchlist: HPE record growth and raised forecast, but stock fell. Watch the Fed, Hormuz, Congress on Nvidia and the Bank of Korea hike on Thursday.

title: Briefing – Monday, 23 November 2026
notes:
- Core chain: AI and chip selloff, Nasdaq 100 down 5.6 percent, Nikkei down 5.1 percent, Kospi down 2.8 percent, then Europe down 2 to 2.8 percent on Friday.
- VIX at 35.9, up 26 percent on the day and 86 percent in five days.
- Bonds rallied: US 10-year 4.91 percent, down 14 bp; Bund 10-year 3.37 percent, down 5 bp. Safe-haven flows, but funding costs remain high.
- Oil: Brent 90.2 dollars, down 2.5 percent; Houthi claim on Rabigh refinery; TTF gas 88.5, up 4.7 percent Friday.
- Gold up 2.9 percent to 3,617 dollars but down 6.1 percent over five days; copper down 7.9 percent over five days.
- Futures bounce: S&P up 2.2 percent, Nasdaq up 3.0 percent, but both still down about 5 percent over the week.
- Sensitivity model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 58 bp; energy about plus 40 bp and commodities about plus 33 bp versus market; weak fit.
- Risks: US probe of Megaspeed in the Nvidia chip case, suppliers halting Southeast Asia shipments, thin Thanksgiving-week liquidity.

title: Briefing – Friday, 20 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: AI sell-off becomes global de-risking. Anthropic IPO up seventeen percent on day one, yet Nasdaq 100 down two point two percent and S&P 500 down two percent.
- Trigger chain: Huang resignation, subpoena, Nvidia down 669 billion dollars in six days, AMD down over seven percent, Intuit weak outlook.
- Asia: Kospi down five point seven percent, Nikkei down four point seven, Hang Seng down two point one. SoftBank down over sixteen percent. Worst week since 2020.
- Rates and FX: US ten-year at five point one percent, dollar near 19-month high, Japan core inflation up and rate-hike expectations firm. Bund ten-year at three point four percent.
- Commodities: gold down four point five percent, copper down two point eight percent and ten percent on the week, Brent at ninety dollars.
- VIX at twenty-eight point four, up fifty-two percent in five days.
- Walmart: EPS 0.65 vs 0.64 estimate, outlook raised, diesel cost hit of 2 billion dollars, stock down about one percent.
- Model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 105 basis points. Telecom, utilities, healthcare, real estate favored; tech, industrials, resources, luxury lag.

title: Briefing – Thursday, 19 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: hawkish Fed (Waller half-point talk, Barr) plus AI wobble squeezes risk. US 10-year at 5.1 percent, VIX 24.6, up 40 percent in five days.
- Nvidia fell after earnings on CEO exit and succession, China and export-control worries, dragging CoreWeave and Iren. Microsoft down nearly 9 percent from its record.
- Anthropic IPO over 81 billion dollars, with a muted Asian reaction. AI debt hedging is building.
- Palo Alto raised its outlook and bought Applied Compute for 4.5 billion dollars, showing demand in AI security.
- Consumer: Target, TJX and Lowe's strong. Walmart reports today.
- Brent 89.3 dollars, down 2.9 percent. TTF down 5.3 percent. Copper down 8 percent over 5 days. Iran strike reports are an oil risk.
- Bund 10-year 3.41 percent, up 2 basis points. EUR/USD about 1.10. Dollar near a 19-month high.
- Model (historical, Hang Seng-driven): Stoxx 600 about minus 23 basis points. Commodities minus 40, luxury minus 37, tech minus 15, utilities plus 19, telecom plus 10 versus market.

title: Briefing – Wednesday, 18 November 2026
notes:
- Nvidia: EPS 2.68 vs 2.47 (+8.4%), guide about 130bn dollars, stock about minus 0.4% as CEO exit, SEC probe and governance dominate.
- Kress: "disciplined" financing of neoclouds, so circular AI funding worries persist. Congress pushes China chip export curbs.
- Rates: US 10-year about 5.1%, Fed's Williams sees more hikes, BofA flags a possible 50bp hike in December. Dollar near 19-month high.
- Oil shock: Brent about 93 dollars, Iran strikes in Kuwait and Bahrain, Hormuz standoff. Chain: oil, then inflation, then yields, then funding costs for small and mid caps, then capex.
- VIX 25.5 (+11% on day, +31% over five days). S&P minus 1.0%, Nasdaq 100 minus 0.7%.
- Europe yesterday: Euro Stoxx 50 minus 2.2%, DAX minus 2.1%, Stoxx 600 minus 1.8%. Bund 10-year about 3.4%.
- Model (rule of thumb, R-squared 0.22 for the Stoxx 600): Stoxx 600 about minus 20bp, luxury versus market about minus 30bp, resources versus market about plus 4bp.
- Watch: Trump, Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, Anthropic IPO on Nov 19, Gulf escalation, Target earnings.

title: Briefing – Tuesday, 17 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: AI jitters plus hawkish rates plus a strong dollar. Bonds are not offering their usual cushion.
- Wall Street Monday: S&P 500 down 1.9 percent, Nasdaq 100 down 2.7 percent, VIX up 18.7 percent to 22.9.
- Asia: Kospi down 2.0 percent (down 4.6 percent over five days), ASX down 1.8, Nikkei down 1.1, Hang Seng down 0.7.
- Rates: US ten-year at 5.12 percent, down 3.3 basis points. Bund ten-year 3.43 percent, up 2 basis points. RBA sees a fifth hike needed.
- FX: Dollar at a 19-month high on Fed hike bets. EUR/USD 1.10, USD/JPY 159.1.
- Commodities: Brent 91.6 dollars. Gulf tension (third US carrier) versus Q4 surplus forecasts. TTF down 6.8 percent. Gold and copper both down about 3.5 percent over five days.
- Europe: Stoxx 600 down 0.3 percent Monday. Rule of thumb implies a lower open (about minus 57 basis points, R-squared 0.22). Energy relatively favored, resources lagging.
- Catalysts: Disney results before the US open, Nvidia earnings this week (first since Huang's exit). No earnings data since yesterday.

title: Briefing – Monday, 16 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: AI trade fragile into Nvidia earnings Tuesday, with high oil and rising yields leaving little cushion.
- Asia: Kospi down 3.8 percent, Nikkei down 2.3 percent; Nasdaq futures down about 1.0 percent after Nasdaq 100 fell 1.2 percent Friday.
- Rates: US ten-year 5.15 percent, up 5.1 basis points; Bund ten-year 3.41 percent, up 8 basis points. Higher discount rate hurts long-duration tech.
- Japan: Q3 GDP contracted (annualized minus 0.1 percent) as energy subsidies expired; BOJ's Takata wants quick hikes. USD/JPY about 159.4.
- China: October output, retail sales and investment missed; foreign reserve requirement hiked for the first time in five years. Copper down 4.8 percent over five days.
- Oil: Brent 95.5 dollars; Iran rhetoric and the November 19 Shenzhen summit are two-way risks.
- Sensitivity model (historical rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 23 basis points, tech minus 29, industrials minus 25, healthcare plus 21, telecoms plus 21. Low R-squared.
- Europe: Stoxx 600 up 2.4 percent on the week; tech and Asia-exposed industrials most at risk, healthcare and telecoms the tactical defensive.

title: Briefing – Friday, 13 November 2026
notes:
- Thesis: equities absorbed the Nvidia CEO resignation (stock down over four percent, S&P 500 down 0.3 percent, VIX 18.7), but rates are the bigger risk.
- Rates chain: US 10-year up 10.5 basis points to 5.1 percent, 5-year up 11.8, on Fed hike expectations; biggest surge since 2022 per MarketWatch.
- FX chain: higher yields lead to a stronger dollar, EUR/USD 1.106 (down 1.5 percent over 5 days), USD/JPY near 160, Japan's finance minister vows action.
- Asia: Hang Seng down 1.2 percent, Kospi down 1.0, Nikkei up 0.6 (up 6.5 percent over 5 days). Chinese chip shares rallied on the Huang turmoil.
- Earnings: Siemens EPS 3.01 vs 2.81 expected, stock up about 2 percent, record orders, buying Lauterbach. Allianz EPS 7.41 vs 8.17, stock flat.
- AI split: Nebius down 16 percent on higher capex, Cerebras up 17 percent on Microsoft deal.
- Sensitivity model (historical rule of thumb): real estate about minus 24 basis points vs market, commodities minus 20, luxury minus 2.
- Watch: Trump-Xi summit next week, yen intervention risk, Fed commentary, Brent at $95.5.

title: Briefing – Thursday, 12 November 2026
notes:
- CoreWeave beat and raised guidance, stock up more than 24 percent, easing AI spending worries and lifting chips; VIX down about 10 percent to 17.5.
- Nvidia down roughly 8 percent after hours on reports the board may oust Jensen Huang; Nasdaq futures down 1.1 percent, S&P futures down 0.5 percent.
- Chain: Huang's opposition to export controls, U.S. probe into Megaspeed, and possible tighter China chip rules lead to semiconductor policy risk. Kospi down 1.3 percent, Hang Seng down 0.9 percent, Nikkei down 0.8 percent.
- Hot October CPI and Fed hike talk: US 10-year at about 5.0 percent; oil-yield link has broken, so lower oil (Brent about 92 dollars, down 6.6 percent over 5 days) isn't lowering yields.
- Bund 2-year up 7 basis points to 3.08 percent, 10-year up 6 basis points to 3.34 percent: higher funding costs for small and mid caps, capex risk.
- Euro-dollar about 1.108, down 0.8 percent; USD/JPY near 160 with intervention warning and mixed BOJ signals.
- Model (historical rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 plus 8 basis points, luxury minus 6, commodities minus 45 (low R-squared 0.09); futures point the other way.
- Other: Nissan second forecast cut on China, Spain general strike, EU reportedly delaying EV tariff with Britain.

title: Briefing – Wednesday, 11 November 2026
notes:
- Hot October CPI (up 0.4 percent) pushed US 10-year yield up 11.9 basis points to about 4.98 percent; 5-year up 14.8 basis points.
- Fed hike odds for December at 88 percent (CME FedWatch); Goldman sees another hike in March.
- Asia bounced (Kospi up 2.1 percent, Nikkei up 1.2 percent), but Kospi is still down 5.9 percent over five days: oversold repair.
- US futures up (S&P 0.7 percent, Nasdaq 1.4 percent) after Tuesday's small declines.
- Brent around 92 dollars after briefly dipping below 90 on Iran peace hopes; US gasoline below 4 dollars.
- Bund 10-year at 3.28 percent, down 2 basis points: widening US-Europe yield gap, EUR/USD down 0.5 percent to 1.12.
- Model (rule of thumb): Stoxx 600 about minus 6 basis points; real estate relative minus 22 basis points on higher US yields.
- Infineon: EPS 0.60 vs 0.62 estimate (miss of 3.9 percent), stock up 6.3 percent on AI data center demand. CoreWeave beat and raised; Anthropic IPO range 70 to 78 dollars, trading expected Nov 19.

title: Briefing – Tuesday, 10 November 2026
notes:
- Core chain: Brent down about twelve percent in five days, now around ninety-one dollars, so lower inflation and margin pressure, so risk-on relief rally in Asia and the US.
- Asia: Kospi up four point one percent, Nikkei up two point seven, but still down seven point six and four point three over five days. This is a bounce, not a trend.
- Tension: US ten-year at four point nine percent, Bund ten-year at three point three, up three basis points, and the German two-year at three percent, up four. Bonds still price sticky inflation.
- Today's key event: US consumer price report for October, expected to show slower price increases. It tests the rotation trade.
- Nvidia and Huang affair: AMD and Broadcom gained, and the political and governance risk for AI is rising. VIX fell twenty-two percent to about twenty.
- China exports up thirty-five percent, surplus above one trillion dollars. Supports volumes, adds trade friction.
- UniCredit earnings per share two point one five euros versus one eighty-eight expected, a fourteen percent beat, but the stock is down half a percent. Banks may be crowded.
- Rule of thumb: Stoxx 600 about half a percent higher, industrials stronger, telecom, utilities and energy weaker. Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi are a swing factor for defence.
